unit_period_analysis: The unit period is 1 year. The number of unit periods from advance to payment is unit_period = 1, with no fractional unit period.
computation: Actuarial equation: Amount Financed = Payment / (1 + i)^1, where i is the periodic rate. $1000.00 = $1060.00 / (1 + i)^1 => 1 + i = 1.060 => i = 0.06 or 6.00%. Annual Percentage Rate (APR) = periodic rate * number of unit periods per year = 6.00% * 1 = 6.00%.
weakest_point: Simplest possible case; does not test complex fractional unit-period fractions.

unit_period_analysis: The interval between payments is equal (1 month). The unit period is defined as 1 month. The number of unit periods per year (w) is 12. First period is equal to the unit period (fractional period f = 0, full periods t = 1).
computation: Actuarial equation: A = P * [(1 - (1 + i)^-n) / i], where A = 5000.00, P = 439.43, n = 12. Solving 5000 = 439.43 * [(1 - (1 + i)^-12) / i] yields monthly periodic rate i = 0.00833333 (0.833333%). Annual Percentage Rate (APR) = 12 * i = 12 * 0.833333% = 10.00%.
weakest_point: Standard level repayment amortization; does not exercise odd day formulas.

case_name: Irregular First Period with Odd Days (Long First Period)
appendix_basis: Appendix J to Part 1026, Section (b)(5) and (c)(3)
unit_period_analysis: Unit period is 1 month (30 days by Appendix J standard month rules or exact days depending on calculation method; using standard unit period = 1 month = 30 days). The first period is 45 days. Number of full unit periods (t) = 1, fractional period (f) = 15/30 = 0.5.
computation: Actuarial equation: A = sum [ P_k / ((1 + f*i) * (1 + i)^(k-1)) ]. Here A = 1000.00, P_k = 90.00 for k = 1..12, f = 0.5. 1000 = sum_{k=1}^{12} [ 90 / ((1 + 0.5*i) * (1 + i)^(k-1)) ]. Solving for monthly rate i gives i ≈ 0.0117025. APR = 12 * i = 14.043% rounded to nearest quarter of 1% or 0.1% per Regulation Z (14.04% or 14.0%).
weakest_point: Counting convention for odd days in fractional first period (exact day count vs. 30-day month convention under Appendix J rules).

unit_period_analysis: Unit period is 1 month. All intervals are regular unit periods (1 month each, no fractional periods). total periods n = 24.
computation: Actuarial equation: A = sum_{k=1}^{23} [ 110 / (1 + i)^k ] + [ 9000 / (1 + i)^24 ]. For A = 10000, solving for i yields monthly rate i ≈ 0.0063284 (0.63284%). Annual Percentage Rate (APR) = 12 * i = 7.594% -> rounded to nearest 0.125% or 0.1% as required by Reg Z = 7.59%.
weakest_point: Numerical iteration step for non-standard payment stream.
